chief_complaint: sharp shooting pain down the back of right leg to foot after lifting heavy box
hpi_details: 38M warehouse worker reports sudden onset of sharp, electric-shock-like pain shooting from his right buttock down the back of his thigh and calf to his outer foot. Started yesterday after lifting a heavy box.
ideas: thinks he has a herniated disc or pinched nerve
concerns: worried about permanent nerve damage and work disability

clinical_knowledge.topic: Right S1 Lumbar Radiculopathy evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Right S1 Lumbar Radiculopathy is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.

Standard management emphasizes Evidence-based diagnostic and therapeutic protocol for Right S1 Lumbar Radiculopathy secondary to herniated disc, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.

Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.

history.answer: I have this terrible sharp, shooting pain going from my right buttock all the way down the back of my leg to my foot.
It starts deep in my right buttock and shoots straight down the back of my thigh and calf, into the outside of my right foot and little toe.
It started suddenly yesterday afternoon right as I was lifting a heavy box off the floor at work.
It feels like a sharp, electric shock that zaps down the leg, around an 8 out of 10 at its worst.
Bending forward, sitting down, or coughing makes the pain shoot worse, but lying flat on my back with a pillow under my knees eases it slightly.
It does not wake me up spontaneously at night as long as I do not turn or move, and resting flat takes the edge off.
My lower back feels a bit stiff when I first get out of bed for maybe five minutes, but it does not last half an hour and exercise definitely does not help.
Yes, I have numbness and tingling along the outer edge of my right foot and my pinky toe.
My right foot feels slightly weak and awkward when I try to push off the floor or walk on my toes.
No, I have had no trouble controlling my urine or bowel movements, and no leakage or retention.
No, the sensation around my groin and private area feels completely normal.
Walking causes pain, but sitting down or bending forward makes the shooting pain much worse rather than better.
No, I have not had any fever, chills, night sweats, or unexplained weight loss.
No, I have never had cancer or any tumors.
No, I have not had any recent infections, spinal procedures, injections, or illnesses, and I have never used intravenous drugs.
No, I have never taken steroid pills, I do not have weak bones, and I have not had any falls.
No belly pain, no pulsing sensation in my stomach, and no burning or blood when I pee.
No eye redness or pain, no heel pain, no chronic diarrhea, and no skin rashes.
I took a couple of ibuprofen tablets yesterday evening, but they barely took the edge off the shooting pain.
I work in a warehouse doing heavy lifting, loading, and bending all day, and I am very stressed about missing work.
I think I might have slipped a disc or pinched a nerve in my back when lifting that box.
I am terrified that this could cause permanent nerve damage and leave me disabled from working.
I was hoping to get an MRI to see what is damaged in my back and get some strong pain medication.
I have always been healthy and have never had back trouble or chronic illnesses before.
I have never had any surgeries and have never been admitted to a hospital.
I do not take any regular prescription medications or supplements, just the ibuprofen I tried yesterday.
I do not have any allergies to medicines, foods, or latex.
I do not smoke, and I have never smoked.
I only have an occasional beer on the weekends with friends, nothing heavy.
I work full-time as a warehouse stocker, and I live in an apartment with my wife.
My parents are both healthy in their sixties with only mild high blood pressure, and no one has spine problems or cancer.

exam.finding: Patient is an alert, muscular male who appears uncomfortable and shifts his weight to avoid sitting on his right buttock.
Blood pressure 126/82 mmHg, pulse 76 beats per minute, respiratory rate 16 breaths per minute, temperature 36.8°C, and oxygen saturation 99% on room air.
Mild tenderness over the right lumbosacral paraspinal musculature, and passive straight leg raise on the right reproduces shooting electric pain down the posterior leg at 40 degrees.
Active lumbar flexion is markedly restricted and provokes sharp pain radiating down the right leg, while extension and lateral bending are mildly restricted.
Right ankle plantarflexion strength is 4/5, whereas bilateral hip flexion, knee extension, knee flexion, ankle dorsiflexion, and great toe extension are all 5/5.
Decreased sensation to light touch and pinprick along the right lateral foot and fifth digit, with normal sensation throughout all other dermatomes.
Right Achilles deep tendon reflex is diminished at 1+, while the left Achilles reflex and bilateral patellar reflexes are 2+, with bilateral flexor plantar responses.
Normal resting anal sphincter tone with intact voluntary contraction and preserved perianal sensation.
Abdomen is soft and non-tender without guarding, rigidity, or palpable pulsatile masses.
No tenderness elicited with gentle percussion over either costovertebral angle.
Gait is antalgic with reduced stance phase on the right, and the patient has difficulty toe walking on the right side while heel walking is preserved.
